what_its_for: Liraglutide is used for two main purposes. Victoza helps control blood sugar levels in adults and children (10 years and older) with type 2 diabetes, and it may also help lower the risk of heart attack or stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes who have heart disease. Saxenda is used to help with weight loss and weight management in adults and children (12 years and older) who are overweight or obese.
how_to_take: Liraglutide comes as a liquid in a pre-filled pen that you inject under your skin (subcutaneously). You can inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Always rotate your injection sites so you do not inject in the same spot every time. Do NOT inject into a vein or muscle. You do not need to time your injection with meals — you can take it at any time of day, but try to take it at the same time each day. Watch the instructions that come with your pen carefully before using it for the first time.
dosing: For Victoza (diabetes): You will start with a low dose of 0.6 mg once daily for one week. After one week, your doctor will increase your dose to 1.2 mg once daily. If needed, your doctor may increase it further to 1.8 mg once daily. For Saxenda (weight management): You will start at 0.6 mg once daily and your dose will be gradually increased each week until you reach the full dose of 3 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next scheduled dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If you miss more than 3 days of doses, call your doctor before restarting — you may need to restart at a lower dose.
storage: Before first use: Store your liraglutide pen in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze it — if it has been frozen, throw it away. After first use: You can store the pen at room temperature (59°F to 77°F / 15°C to 25°C) OR in the refrigerator for up to 30 days. Always keep the pen cap on when not in use to protect it from light. Do not store the pen with a needle attached. Keep it out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping meals or drastically cutting calories without talking to your doctor first. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar. Do not share your liraglutide pen with anyone else, even if the needle is changed — this can spread infections. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded. Do not use this medication if you or a family member has ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or a condition called Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: a lump or swelling in your neck, hoarse voice, or trouble swallowing (possible thyroid tumor signs); severe stomach pain that does not go away and may spread to your back (possible pancreatitis); signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion (especially if taking with other diabetes medicines); signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing; yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain (possible liver problems); or severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that causes you to lose a lot of fluids.
when_it_works: Liraglutide starts working to lower blood sugar within a few days, but it may take several weeks to see the full effect on your blood sugar levels. For weight loss with Saxenda, most people begin to see some weight loss within the first few weeks, but the full benefit is usually seen after several months of use along with diet and exercise. Your doctor will check your progress at regular visits.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Liraglutide is generally not recommended during pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor right away about safer options. Breastfeeding: It is not known if liraglutide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Victoza can be used in children 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes. Saxenda can be used in children 12 years and older who are obese. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems. Elderly: Older adults can use this medication, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
